questions.question: predict: CSV load karne ke baad `df.shape` aur `df.dtypes` — inme se kaun aage ka code todega, aur kyun?
questions.answer: `dtypes` — jo column numbers dikh raha hai par dtype `object` hai, uspar arithmetic silently galat ya `TypeError` deti hai. Shape theek hone par bhi dtype galat ho sakti hai, isliye dono print karo: `print(df.shape); print(df.dtypes)`.

questions.question: trace: `df.groupby('region')['amount'].sum()` kya return karta hai aur uska index kya hota hai?
questions.answer: Ek Series return hoti hai jiska index unique `region` values hain aur values per-region sums. Flat DataFrame chahiye to `reset_index(name='revenue')` lagao; index ko sort/order ke liye bhi use kar sakte ho (`sort_index()`).

questions.question: why: Merge ke baad row count badh gaya — sabse likely reason?
questions.answer: Join key me duplicates (one-to-many ya many-to-many fan-out): ek left row kai right rows se match kar jati hai. `df[key].duplicated().any()` se check karo, aur duplicated side ko pehle aggregate karke unique karo — phir merge karo.
questions.explanation: Verified: right table me key `1` do baar hone par duplicate_keys() ne `[1]` diya — wahi fan-out ki warning hai. Row counts merge se pehle/baad compare karna must hai.

questions.question: fix: Kaun sa edge case `df['amount'].mean()` ko galat jawab dene par majboor karta hai?
questions.answer: NaN values — `mean()` unhe skip karta hai par `count()` me unhe ginnta hi nahi, isliye numerator aur denominator ka basis alag ho jata hai. Khaali DataFrame par `NaN` aata hai. Decide karo: `skipna=False` (honest NaN) ya pehle `dropna`/`fillna`.
questions.explanation: skipna ka default aksar "theek lagta hai" par report me count mismatch karta hai — isliye null counts ke saath mean print karna achhi aadat hai.

questions.question: design: Data cleaning pipeline me validation kahan lagao?
questions.answer: Har transform ke baad light assertions (shape, null counts, key uniqueness) — ya schema-level check ingestion par. Ye leakage aur silently misaligned columns ko wahi rokta hai jahan wo banta hai, warna bug downstream model metrics me dikhta hai.
questions.explanation: Assert-after-transform pattern: chhoti check chain se galat data aage nahi jaata, aur failure ka location exact milega.

questions.question: tradeoff: Bade CSV me pehle kya optimize karoge: dtype downcast, chunks me read, ya column selection?

questions.question: Datetime handling ke teen zaroori kaam likho.
questions.answer: Parse with errors='coerce', timezone-aware ya naive consistently rakho (mix mat karo), aur resample/rolling ke liye DatetimeIndex set karo. Saath me UTC me store karo aur display par local time.
questions.explanation: Coerce + consistent tz + index.

questions.question: Categorical dtype ka fayda kya hai?
questions.answer: Memory bachti hai (codes + levels) aur groupby/sort ka order explicit hota hai. Par categories ke bahar naya value NaN ban jaata hai, isliye mode/levels ko validate karo.
questions.explanation: Memory + fixed order, par NaN risk.

questions.question: Memory kam karne ke teen practical tarike likho.
questions.answer: Chhote dtypes (int8/int16, category), sirf zaroori columns load karo (usecols), aur chunked read (chunksize) — plus string columns ko category/string dtype me convert karna.
questions.explanation: Dtype + usecols + chunks.

questions.question: Copy-on-write (pandas 2.0+) ka practical asar kya hai?
questions.answer: Views aur copies ka confusing behaviour kam hota hai: chained assignment silent fail hoti hai (warning/error), aur memory copy tab banti hai jab likhna shuru karo. Isliye explicit .copy() aur .loc assignment best practice hai.
questions.explanation: CoW se silent writes khatam.

questions.question: Rolling aur expanding me farq?
questions.answer: rolling(window=n) fixed window ka aggregate deta hai (moving average), expanding() start se ab tak ka cumulative window deta hai. Dono min_periods se control hote hain (khaali window par NaN).
questions.explanation: Rolling fixed, expanding cumulative.

questions.question: idxmax aur nlargest me kab kaunsa?
questions.answer: idxmax() max value ka index deta hai (ek per axis); nlargest(n) top-n rows ek hi call me deta hai (grouped top-N ke liye groupby + nlargest ya sort+head).
questions.explanation: Index chahiye → idxmax, top-N rows → nlargest.

questions.question: describe() me median aur quantiles kaise milte hain?
questions.answer: describe() default count/mean/std/min/25/50/75/max deta hai (50% = median); custom ke liye describe(percentiles=[.9, .99]) ya quantile([0.5, 0.9]). Non-numeric columns ke liye value_counts zyada useful hai.
questions.explanation: 50% quantile = median.

questions.question: Grouped result ko original rows par wapas kaise laate ho (broadcast)?
questions.answer: transform ya map + merge: df['grp_mean'] = df.groupby('grp')['x'].transform('mean') — same index broadcast ho jaata hai, jo z-score/normalization ke liye perfect hai.
questions.explanation: transform = group stat back on rows.

questions.question: Parquet aur CSV me production me kaunsa choose karoge?
questions.answer: Parquet: columnar, typed, compressed, fast partial reads (columns chuno) — analytics/repeated loads ke liye better. CSV: interchange aur human-readable, par types guess hote hain aur bada file slow.
questions.explanation: Analytics → Parquet, interchange → CSV.

questions.question: Duplicate rows ka standard treatment likho.
questions.answer: Pehle detect: df.duplicated(subset=[...]).sum(), phir business rule decide: exact duplicates drop, ya keep='last' (latest wins). Purge ke baad row count aur affected keys report karo.
questions.explanation: Detect → rule → purge + report.

questions.question: Production pandas pipeline ko reproducible kaise rakhte ho?
questions.answer: Input snapshots (Parquet + hash), deterministic sorts, explicit dtypes, fixed seeds aur validation assertions (row counts, null rates, ranges) — pipeline ko code + schema version ke saath pin karo.
questions.explanation: Snapshot + dtypes + assertions.

questions.question: Real-world: outlier detection karo IQR method se aur flag column add karo (delete nahi).
questions.answer:
import pandas as pd

def flag_outliers(df, col, k=1.5):
    q1, q3 = df[col].quantile([0.25, 0.75])
    iqr = q3 - q1
    lo, hi = q1 - k * iqr, q3 + k * iqr
    df[f'{col}_outlier'] = (df[col] < lo) | (df[col] > hi)
    return df, (lo, hi)
questions.explanation: Flag karo, delete nahi — analyst decide karega.

questions.question: Checkpoint: DataFrame ke chaar core inspection methods likho.
questions.answer: head/tail (peek), info (dtype + nulls), describe (stats), shape/columns (structure).
questions.explanation: Baseline recall.

questions.question: Checkpoint: missing value ke chaar treatment options likho.
questions.answer: Drop rows/columns, impute (median/mode/fill), forward/backward fill (time series), aur indicator column + impute (missingness ko feature banana).
questions.explanation: Chaaron ka use-case alag hai.

questions.question: Checkpoint: groupby ke saath teen step likho jo hamesha karte ho.
questions.answer: 1) groupby keys validate karo (null keys ka kya hoga). 2) agg/transform se summary nikalo. 3) result reset_index aur row count cross-check karo.
questions.explanation: Validate → aggregate → verify.

questions.question: Checkpoint: merge ke chaar types aur ek-ek ka output likho.
questions.answer: inner (dono me match), left (left ki saari rows), right (right ki saari rows), outer (sab). Non-matching side me NaN aate hain.
questions.explanation: Join family.

questions.question: Checkpoint: loc ke saath safe assignment ka pattern likho.
questions.answer: df.loc[df['amount'] < 0, 'amount'] = 0 — ek hi step me row filter + column + value, isliye chained-assignment ka silent fail nahi hota.
questions.explanation: Loc me single-step assignment.

questions.question: Checkpoint: datetime ke teen must-do likho.
questions.answer: parse_dates/errors='coerce', consistent timezone (UTC store), aur .dt accessor se components nikalna.
questions.explanation: Parse + tz + dt accessor.

questions.question: Checkpoint: dtypes ko explicit rakhne ke teen fayde likho.
questions.answer: Predictable memory, correct comparisons/sorting (string vs number), aur merge/join mismatches se bachav (int vs str key).
questions.explanation: Explicit dtype = kam surprises.

questions.question: Checkpoint: top-N per group nikalne ka pattern likho.
questions.answer: df.sort_values('amount', ascending=False).groupby('group').head(3) — ya groupby('group')['amount'].nlargest(3).
questions.explanation: Sort + head per group.

questions.question: Checkpoint: text cleaning ke chaar steps likho.
questions.answer: Type cast (astype(str)), case fold, whitespace strip, aur Unicode/punctuation normalize — tay karo kis level tak normalize karna hai.
questions.explanation: Cast → lower → strip → normalize.

questions.question: Checkpoint: result ko validate karne ke teen assertions likho.
questions.answer: Row count expectation (ya delta), null rate per column, aur key uniqueness (duplicated().sum() == 0).
questions.explanation: Asserts pipeline ko honest rakhte hain.

questions.question: Checkpoint: Parquet over CSV ke teen fayde likho.
questions.answer: Columnar (sirf zaroori columns padho), typed (dtype guess nahi), compressed aur fast — plus schema metadata.
questions.explanation: Typed + columnar + fast.

questions.question: Checkpoint: pivot_table ke teen main parameters likho.
questions.answer: index (rows), columns (pivot keys), values + aggfunc (kya aggregate karna hai); saath me fill_value aur margins.
questions.explanation: Index/columns/values+aggfunc.

questions.question: Checkpoint: pipeline ke teen reproducibility practices likho.
questions.answer: Input snapshot + hash, deterministic sorts/seeds, aur schema/dtype validation assertions.
questions.explanation: Snapshot + determinism + validation.

questions.question: Checkpoint: chained assignment ka warning message aur sahi fix likho.
questions.answer: SettingWithCopyWarning → fix: df.loc[mask, 'col'] = value (single step) ya pehle explicit .copy() lo.
questions.explanation: Ek step me likho.

questions.question: Checkpoint: resample ke liye kya prerequisite hai?
questions.answer: DatetimeIndex (ya column ko DatetimeIndex banana) aur ek aggregation function; missing buckets ke liye fill_value/ffill decide karo.
questions.explanation: Time index ke bina resample nahi.

questions.question: Checkpoint: describe() non-numeric column par kya deta hai?
questions.answer: count, unique, top, freq (categorical summary) — numeric stats nahi. Numeric chahiye to column ko convert karo ya value_counts use karo.
questions.explanation: Object column ka apna summary.

questions.question: Checkpoint: apply vs vectorized ka decision rule ek line me likho.
questions.answer: Agar operation built-in vectorized form me likha ja sakta hai (arithmetic/where/str/dt) to woh use karo; apply sirf tab jab custom per-row Python logic lazmi ho.
questions.explanation: Vectorized pehle, apply last.

questions.question: Checkpoint: duplicate handling ke teen steps likho.
questions.answer: Detect (duplicated().sum()), rule decide karo (keep first/last/aggregate), aur purge ke baad row count + affected keys log karo.
questions.explanation: Detect → rule → log.

questions.question: Checkpoint: groupby me dropna=False kyun zaroori ho sakta hai?
questions.answer: Default me null group keys drop ho jaate hain, isliye 'kitne orders me customer missing hai' jaisa sawal ka jawab gayab ho jaata hai — dropna=False se woh group dikhta hai.
questions.explanation: Null group ko visible rakho.

questions.question: Project defense: 'Tumne pandas use kiya, SQL kyun nahi?'
questions.answer: Decision data size aur workflow par thi: data files (CSV/Parquet) aur join/feature prep par pandas fast iterate karne deta hai; jab data database me ho ya scale badhe, wahi transform SQL me chala diya jata hai. Dono jagah logic single source me rakhne ki koshish karta hoon.
questions.explanation: Tool choice data ke location se justify karo.

questions.question: Project defense: 'Tumhare analysis me missing data ka kya effect pada — usse quantify karo.'
questions.answer: Missing rate 3.2% tha (mostly 'phone' column). Numeric fields par median imputation ki aur ek indicator column rakha; sensitive metric par effect compare kiya (imputation ke bina vs ke saath 1.1% difference), isliye conclusion robust tha.
questions.explanation: Missing rate + sensitivity check.

questions.question: Project defense: 'Tumhare dashboard ka metric reproducible hai — koi aur wahi number nikaal sakta hai?'
questions.answer: Haan: definition docs me likhi hai (filters, status, date bounds), code versioned pipeline me hai with fixed dtypes/seeds, aur input snapshot hash ke saath stored hai — isliye same snapshot se same number nikalta hai.
questions.explanation: Definition + code + snapshot.

questions.question: Project defense: 'Outliers ko tumne delete kiya ya rakha — kyun?'
questions.answer: Delete nahi kiya; flag karke rakhe (IQR method) aur sensitivity analysis dikhaya: outliers ke saath mean 12% upar tha par median stable tha, isliye reporting me median + flagged view rakha. Deleting silently conclusion badal deti hai.
questions.explanation: Flag + sensitivity, silent delete nahi.

questions.question: Project defense: 'Tumne pipeline me kaunsi validation lagayi jo production me bug pakadti hai?'
questions.answer: Schema + range + null assertions pipeline ke entry par: expected columns, dtype checks, amount >= 0, aur date range validation. Ek baar ek upstream column rename ne pipeline ko foran fail kiya instead of silently 0 revenue.
questions.explanation: Fail fast assertions.

questions.question: Project defense: 'Ek bade CSV par tumhara code kab fail hoga aur mitigation kya hai?'
questions.answer: Jab data RAM se bada ho jaaye (ya join me row explosion ho). Mitigation: chunked read + aggregated state, usecols aur chhote dtypes, aur bade joins ke liye DuckDB/polars. Row count sanity check har step par.
questions.explanation: Chunk + engine switch + sanity checks.

questions.question: Project defense: 'Tumne feature engineering me leakage kaise rok'',' kya bollo?
questions.answer: Time-based split use kiya, target-derived features nahi banaye, aur scalers/imputers sirf training fold par fit kiye (pipeline me). Group leakage (same user train aur test me) ko bhi group split se roka.
questions.explanation: Split discipline = no leakage.

questions.question: Project defense: 'Groupby ke baad row count mismatch aaya to tum kaise debug karte ho?'
questions.answer: Expected vs actual rows compare karta hoon: null keys (dropna default), unexpected duplicates (validate param), aur filter order. Praktik fix: dropna=False ya key cleanup, phir merge ke saath re-verify counts.
questions.explanation: Count mismatch = key hygiene ka sawal.

questions.question: Project defense: 'Data quality ka ownership kaun karta hai — tumhara pipeline ya source team?'
questions.answer: Contract shared hai: source team schema promise karti hai (versioned), pipeline contract assert karti hai (fail + alert), aur mismatch par data contract discussion hoti hai. Silent coercion nahi karte — warna source team ko pata hi nahi chalega.
questions.explanation: Contract + assertion + escalation.

questions.question: Project defense: 'Explain how you tuned performance — numbers ke saath.'
questions.answer: Profiling se pata chala 80% time ek apply call me ja raha tha. Usko str.contains + np.where vectorization me badla: 8.2s se 0.3s (27x), memory stable. Har step ke baad timing log kiya, isliye claim measurable hai.
questions.explanation: Profile → vectorize → measured delta.

questions.question: Project defense: 'Tumhare joins row count kyun badha diya aur kaise fix kiya?'
questions.answer: Right table me duplicate keys thi, isliye many-to-many join ne rows multiply kar diye. Fix: right side ko groupby se ek row per key banao (ya drop_duplicates with rule) aur merge me validate='many_to_one' lagao taaki ye dobara na ho.
questions.explanation: Duplicate keys + validate param.

questions.question: Project defense: 'Column-level documentation kahan rakhi hai?'
questions.answer: Schema registry (dtype, meaning, allowed range, owner) repo me JSON/YAML me hai, aur pipeline usi se validation rules generate karta hai — docs aur code ek jagah rehte hain, isliye drift nahi hota.
questions.explanation: Schema as code.

questions.question: Project defense: 'Ek stake holder ka number tumhare number se alag hai — kaise resolve karoge?'
questions.answer: Definition compare karke shuru karta hoon: date bounds, status filters, refund treatment, aur grain (orders vs customers). Phir ek chhoti reproducible example par dono queries chala kar farq dikhata hoon aur definition library me lock karta hoon.
questions.explanation: Definition diff → evidence → lock.

questions.question: Project defense: 'Dataset 10x bade ho jaaye to architecture kaise badloge?'
questions.answer: Pandas single node chhodkar DuckDB/polars (out-of-core) aur pre-aggregated tables par shift; raw data partition by date; notebook logic ko versioned jobs me convert karo with idempotent outputs aur snapshots.
questions.explanation: Out-of-core + partitioned + idempotent.

questions.question: Project defense: 'Agar tumhara pipeline silently galat number de de to pakadne ka mechanism kya hai?'
questions.answer: Metric-level monitors: row count delta, revenue distribution shift, day-over-day jump alert, aur 'as of' freshness check. Ek baar missing status filter se revenue 20% upar aa gaya tha, tab se yeh alert active hai.
questions.explanation: Monitors + past incident.

questions.question: Project defense: 'Interviewer poochta hai tumne kya automate kiya' — jawab?
questions.answer: Manual Excel steps ko reproducible pipeline me convert kiya: raw → validated → aggregated daily table, jisme assertions aur alert lagte hain. Result: 4 ghante ka weekly manual work ~2 minute ka scheduled job ban gaya, aur numbers consistent.
questions.explanation: Automation + time saved + consistency.

questions.question: Project defense: 'Do analysts ka farq wala number ka root cause kya nikla aur usse kya badla?'
questions.answer: Root cause timezone tha (ek UTC me group kar raha tha, doosra local me), isliye day boundary shift ho gayi thi. Badla: UTC store + explicit tz handling, definition docs me note, aur ek regression test jo known fixture par daily counts assert karta hai.
questions.explanation: Silent tz bug ko test se band karo.

questions.question: Project defense: 'Tumhara analysis kitna trustworthy hai — ek limitation batao.'
questions.answer: Limitation: attribution window 7 din tha, isliye long-delay conversions undercounted hain. Isliye report me method + window likha hai aur sensitivity (14/30 din window) appendix me hai — number ke saath assumption bhi bhejta hoon.
questions.explanation: Limitation openly declare karo.

questions.question: Interview: 'merge me left_on/right_on aur suffixes kab use karoge?'
questions.answer: Jab dono tables me key column ka naam alag ho (left_on='user_id', right_on='id') aur non-key columns ka naam clash kare to suffixes=('_left', '_right') do — warna pandas silently _x/_y laga deta hai jo code me read karna confusing hota hai.
questions.explanation: Alag keys + explicit suffixes.

questions.question: Checkpoint: DataFrame copy karne ke teen tarike aur unka farq likho.

questions.question: Project defense: 'Tumhare analysis code ka kaunsa hissa test kiya aur kaunsa deliberately nahi?'
questions.answer: Transformation functions (cleaning, aggregation, metric calc) unit tests se cover kiye chhote fixtures ke saath; plotting aur one-off exploration untested hai kyunki woh deliverable nahi. Metric layer par regression test hai jo known numbers assert karta hai.

questions.question: Project defense: 'Data me PII column tha — tumne kaise handle kiya?'

questions.question: Explain: Series ko basic level par explain karo aur ek AI/data use case batao.
questions.answer: Series: Pandas labeled 1D data structure. Example: pd.Series([1,2]). Pitfall: index alignment surprises.
questions.explanation: USE / IMPACT: single column analysis me.

questions.question: Define: DataFrame ko basic level par explain karo aur ek AI/data use case batao.
questions.answer: DataFrame: labeled 2D table with columns/index. Example: pd.DataFrame(data). Pitfall: dtype/missingness/index assumptions.
questions.explanation: USE / IMPACT: tabular data manipulation and analytics me.

questions.question: Differentiate: read_csv() ko basic level par explain karo aur ek AI/data use case batao.
questions.answer: read_csv(): CSV ko DataFrame me load karta hai. Example: pd.read_csv("sales.csv"). Pitfall: type inference/encoding/schema drift.
questions.explanation: USE / IMPACT: analytics ingestion ke liye.

questions.question: Predict: info() ko basic level par explain karo aur ek AI/data use case batao.
questions.answer: info(): columns, dtypes, non-null counts ka compact profile. Example: df.info(). Pitfall: not a full data-quality report.
questions.explanation: USE / IMPACT: data quality triage ke first step me.

questions.question: Identify: describe() ko basic level par explain karo aur ek AI/data use case batao.
questions.answer: describe(): numeric/distribution summary statistics. Example: df.describe(). Pitfall: categorical summaries need explicit handling.
questions.explanation: USE / IMPACT: EDA me outliers and scale inspect karne ke liye.

questions.question: Apply: loc/iloc ko basic level par explain karo aur ek AI/data use case batao.
questions.answer: loc/iloc: label-based vs integer-position indexing. Example: df.loc[mask,["a"]]. Pitfall: mixing label and position semantics.
questions.explanation: USE / IMPACT: safe row/column selection me.
